target_customer: Security and platform teams at software companies that need least privilege access control over databases, internal APIs, infrastructure and AI agents
problem: Access permissions rarely match the work people and now AI agents actually need to do, so sensitive data is overexposed and hard to audit.
business_model: B2B SaaS security platform (proxies, PAM, policy control plane)
product_category: cybersecurity / access control and PAM for humans and AI agents

founders.name: Mokhtar Bacha
previous_startups: Maytana (cash management platform, pivoted into Formal)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2024-11 says he joined ConsenSys as a teenager, applied to YC as a solo founder at 19 with Maytana, and was 24 at publication. Education not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Protocol-aware proxies for many databases, SSH, Kubernetes and APIs that must inspect individual calls with low latency are hard to build for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Deep deployment in the network path and many protocol parsers create switching costs, but established access vendors can add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition found; access management vendors and AI gateway startups keep adding agent controls.

market_need_then: Growing data security and access governance demand; by 2024 customers such as Gusto, Notion and Ramp were named, and the 2025 to 2026 AI agent wave created new demand for agent least privilege.

branding.domain_note: Moved from joinformal.com to formal.ai, which now redirects; purchase details not found.

rebrands.why: not stated; domain change only, dated approximately

brand_strength.rationale: Short real word name but generic and hard to search; no press about the brand itself or community evidence found.

pivots.why: TechCrunch says Maytana pivoted into Formal; reason not given

outcome_analysis: Formal began as the YC company Maytana, pivoted to access security around 2023, raised a seed round led by Thrive Capital in late 2023 and came out of stealth in November 2024 with named customers such as Gusto, Notion and Ramp. In 2026 it sells network security for AI agents with customers like Cursor. No later round or exit was found, so the outcome is still open.
notes: Directory lists batch Summer 2020, consistent with the Maytana application at 19, but the YC page says founded 2023 and the Formal product dates from 2023, so as_of is set to the batch month and the competitor list is left empty: searches returned only undated vendor comparison pages for StrongDM and Teleport, and no source dated near 2020 or 2023 named a rival. Seed amount conflict: TechCrunch says $5.8M, Formal's own blog says $6.8M; recorded the TechCrunch figure. Seed announced 2024-11 but TechCrunch dates the round late 2023. A third-party site also lists the batch as S20; not relied on. Copyright holder on site is Maytana, Inc. rebrand date for the domain is approximate.
